newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WINS RACE, WIBERG CLINCHES OVERALL CROWN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WINS RACE, WIBERG CLINCHES OVERALL CROWN.

text.p: Katja Seizinger of Germany skied a near-perfect race Friday to claim victory in the women's World Cup super-g at Mammoth Mountain, but Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg nailed down the season's overall title with a third-place finish.
Taking an aggressive line in the steep first section of the 35-gate course, Seizinger set a pace that no one could match. She claimed gold with a winning time of one minute 16.08 seconds.
Hilde Gerg of Germany finished second in 1:17.67, just ahead of Wiberg, whose 1:17.72 clocking gave her an insurmountable lead in the overall World Cup Standings with 1,615 points.

The super-g, originally scheduled for Thursday, was postponed a day by high winds on the course. Perfect conditions met the racers Friday morning and the slalom that had been set for Friday was going ahead later in the day as planned.

But even if Seizinger, who now has 1,104 overall points, wins the afternoon slalom and all of her races at the Finals next week in Vail, she would come up 11 points short of Wiberg's current overall total.
Wiberg maintained her super-g lead with 449 points, but has yet to lock up that title. Gerg stands second on 410 points and Seizinger moved into third place with 374 points.
Defending super-g champion Isolde Kostner of Italy moved back into the fourth place on 355 points after placing fourth Friday.
